purpose: Sourced foundation for the Kona race-week companion and Island Stories wing. Editorial history/culture is kept separate from practical trip-planning metadata.

population.note: County-level context for the island of Hawaiʻi; not a Kailua-Kona city estimate.

principles: Hawaiʻi is a living place and home, not a race backdrop.
Use Native Hawaiian names and diacritics where source material provides them.
Culturally significant sites require context and respectful-visit guidance.
Visitor planning never overrides official closures, safety advice, access rules or local guidance.
The app stores saved places locally by default and does not track a visitor's live location.

stories.title: Voyaging & Kānaka Maoli
stories.summary: Native Hawaiians navigated to and flourished in the Hawaiian Islands for centuries, developing cultural traditions and lifeways that remain living practices today.

stories.title: Royal Kona
stories.summary: Kailua-Kona includes places associated with Hawaiian royalty; Kamehameha I spent his later years at Kamakahonu near Kailua Pier.

stories.title: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau
stories.summary: The National Historical Park preserves major traditional Hawaiian sites, including the puʻuhonua, Royal Grounds and monumental Great Wall.

stories.title: Land shaped by volcanoes
stories.summary: Hawaiʻi Island includes Kīlauea, Maunaloa, Maunakea, Hualālai and Kohala; volcanic landscapes shape both the island and the race environment.

stories.title: Kona coffee country
stories.summary: Kona coffee is grown on upland slopes in North and South Kona, where elevation, cloud cover and volcanic soils support coffee farming.

Curated half-day/full-day collections with clear time and travel assumptions.
Race-week overlays for course context, closures and spectator planning, only from current official sources.
